covers: JSE session to 14:30 SAST, Thursday 29 October 2026; updates the 13:15 edition
headline: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for $17 billion; Lilly beats and lifts outlook; SA economy about 5% bigger after rebasing
summary: Statistics South Africa's move to a 2022 base year puts last year's nominal GDP at R8.04 trillion, up from R7.64 trillion, which should flatter debt-to-GDP and other ratios (Reuters via Investing.com, 29 Oct), and comes on the same day producer inflation jumped to 6.2% from 5.0% (FX.co, 29 Oct); the rand is near R16.65 per dollar (Trading Economics, 29 Oct). In the US, DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for $65 a share, about $17 billion (DoorDash, 29 Oct), Eli Lilly beat forecasts and raised its revenue outlook to $91–92 billion, and ServiceNow was about 19% lower before the open on an earnings miss (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct); GDP and PCE data were due at 14:30 SAST and the ECB decides at 15:15 SAST. Brent is near $114 after a reported US approach to Iran (The National, 29 Oct), and Shell beat profit forecasts on a record refining margin (Reuters via Finimize, 29 Oct).

items.title: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for $65 a share, about $17 billion
items.summary: DoorDash signed a deal on 29 October to buy Instacart owner Maplebear at $65.00 a share, an equity value of about $17 billion. Holders can take cash, 0.3372 DoorDash shares, or a mix, with at least 75% of the total paid in cash. The price is 26% above Instacart's 22 October close, before deal reports, and about 11% above its last close. Closing is expected at the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, subject to Instacart shareholder and competition approvals in the US, Canada and Israel; holders of about 19% of Instacart have agreed to vote for it. (DoorDash, 29 Oct 2026; InsideArbitrage, 29 Oct 2026)

items.title: Eli Lilly beats and raises 2026 revenue outlook to $91–92 billion; shares up about 4% before the open
items.summary: Lilly's third-quarter revenue rose 39% to $24.4 billion against about $22.6 billion expected, and adjusted earnings per share were $7.48 against $6.35 expected. Mounjaro sales rose 65% to $10.7 billion and Zepbound 49% to $5.35 billion. The full-year revenue forecast was raised to $91–92 billion. Shares were about 4% higher before the open. (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct 2026)

items.title: SA economy about 5% bigger after Stats SA rebasing: 2025 GDP now R8.04 trillion
items.summary: Statistics South Africa moved the GDP base year from 2015 to 2022, lifting last year's nominal GDP to R8.04 trillion (about $483 billion) from R7.64 trillion. All 10 sectors were revised up, led by mining, finance and trade, and newly measured activity such as self-generated electricity, illegal mining and e-hailing was added. Economists say a bigger GDP base makes debt-to-GDP and deficit ratios look better; it does not change the debt itself. (Reuters via Investing.com, 29 Oct 2026)

items.title: ECB President Lagarde to step down on 7 February 2027, about eight months early
items.summary: The ECB said Christine Lagarde will leave on 7 February 2027; her term was due to end in October 2027. No reason was given; reports link her to the World Economic Forum. Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot are named as leading candidates. The news lands before today's ECB rate decision at 15:15 SAST and her press conference at 15:45 SAST. (Global Banking & Finance Review, 29 Oct 2026)

items.title: SA producer inflation jumps to 6.2% in September, above the 5.7% expected
items.summary: Producer price inflation rose to 6.2% year on year in September from 5.0% in August, according to data released on 29 October (FX.co, 29 Oct 2026). Economists polled by Reuters had expected 5.7% (Reuters via Finimize, 29 Oct 2026). Higher factory-gate prices can feed into consumer inflation, which was 4.5% in September; the breakdown by product will be added once verified.

items.title: Shell beats: Q3 adjusted earnings $10.81 billion vs $10.33 billion expected; buyback raised to $5 billion
items.summary: Shell's adjusted third-quarter earnings were $10.81 billion, above the $10.33 billion analysts expected and nearly double a year earlier, on a record refining margin of $42 a barrel (from $11.6 a year earlier). Quarterly buybacks rise to $5 billion from $3 billion (Reuters via Finimize; Rallies, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Alphabet misses on profit and burns cash; shares down about 10% after hours
items.summary: Alphabet's third-quarter adjusted EPS was $2.67 against $3.02 expected and revenue $127.6 billion against $128.2 billion (LSEG); advertising revenue of $82 billion missed the $83.4 billion estimate as search-ad growth slowed more than expected. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.71 billion with a $561 billion backlog, but free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion against expectations of about break-even. Alphabet kept 2026 capital spending at $195–$205 billion and said spending will rise significantly in 2027. The shares fell about 10% after hours, wiping out close to $400 billion in market value (Reuters via Investing.com and Yahoo Finance, 28–29 Oct). This replaces our evening note, which described revenue as roughly in line before the profit figures were verified.

items.title: US futures: Nasdaq down 1.1%, S&P 500 down 0.3%, Dow up 0.6%
items.summary: On Thursday morning Nasdaq futures were down 1.14% at 29,637.75 and S&P 500 futures down 0.30% at 7,760, while Dow futures rose 0.57% to 52,995; the 10-year Treasury yield was 5.05% and WTI December crude was down 1.35% at $101.39 (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct). Overnight, Nasdaq 100 futures had been down 1.2%, led by Alphabet's 9.8% after-hours fall (Investing.com, 28 Oct).

items.title: Microsoft capex $45.2 billion, below the $50.7 billion expected; CoreWeave and Nebius drop
items.summary: Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter capital spending including finance leases was $45.2 billion against a $50.7 billion StreetAccount estimate and its own target of about $50 billion; CFO Amy Hood said some third-party capacity deliveries were delayed. Alphabet's quarterly capex of $51.36 billion was also below the $55.09 billion expected. In overnight trade CoreWeave fell 5.8%, Nebius 6.3%, IREN 5.3% and Applied Digital 4.3% (Stocktwits, 28 Oct).

items.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted a hike
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% on 28 October in a 10–2 vote; Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a 0.25-point hike (American Banker, 28 Oct). Chair Kevin Warsh gave no guidance on December; the 10-year Treasury yield went back above 5% after his comments before easing, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a December hike at 83.5%, up from 72.8% (Investing.com, 28 Oct). By early Thursday in Asia, traders priced about 78% (Free Malaysia Today, 29 Oct).
items.source: American Banker; AFP via Yahoo News; HousingWire, 28 Oct 2026

items.title: Wall Street closes slightly higher after the Fed: Dow +0.19% at 52,480; S&P 500 +0.28%; Nasdaq +0.27%
items.summary: The Dow closed up 0.19% at 52,479.62, the S&P 500 up 0.28% at 7,744.28 and the Nasdaq up 0.27% at 26,549.85 after the Fed held rates in a 10–2 vote; the 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.05% (Yahoo Finance, 28 Oct).

items.title: Bank of Canada raises its rate to 2.50%, its first hike since 2023, and warns more may be needed
items.summary: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% from 2.25% on 28 October; markets had priced about a 78% chance. It said "There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully," and lifted its inflation forecasts to 2.9% for 2026 (from 2.5%) and 3.1% for 2027 (from 2.0%), mainly because of energy prices (investingLive, 28 Oct). A second G7 central bank tightening on oil-driven inflation adds weight to tonight's Fed decision.

items.title: Rand near R16.65 per dollar, its weakest since early October
items.summary: The rand traded at about 16.65 per dollar on 29 October, about 0.3% weaker on the day and close to its weakest level since early October, pressured by a firmer dollar, lower gold and platinum prices and high oil (Trading Economics, 29 Oct 2026). Earlier, at 08:07 SAST, it was 0.4% weaker at 16.65 and the 2035 government bond yield fell 2.5 basis points to 8.56% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 29 Oct 2026).
items.source: Trading Economics; Reuters via CNBC Africa, 29 Oct 2026

items.title: Money supply and credit growth slow in September
items.summary: M3 money supply growth slowed to 7.93% year on year in September from 8.89% in August, and private-sector credit growth slowed to 6.23% from 7.47%; trade and budget balance data are due Friday (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Moody's: budget update is credit positive; Ba2 rating, positive outlook
items.summary: In a report released on Monday, Moody's said the medium-term budget policy statement was credit positive, citing continued fiscal consolidation despite higher oil prices; the 2026 consolidated deficit target was cut to 3.9% of GDP from 4.0%, helped by a R17.1 billion upward revision to tax revenue. Moody's sees debt at 84.9% of GDP by fiscal 2028, down from about 86.8% in fiscal 2025, but said interest absorbed 18.8% of revenue in fiscal 2025. There was no rating action (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 26 Oct).

items.title: Oil slips: Brent down about 1.1% to $114.10 after Vance letter to Iran
items.summary: Brent fell to $114.10 a barrel early on Thursday from Wednesday's $115.32 settlement, and WTI traded above $101 after closing at $102.78, after the Wall Street Journal reported Vice President Vance wrote to Iran's Mohsen Rezaei to revive talks; President Trump downplayed the outreach (The National, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Dollar steady after the Fed; euro $1.1134, yen ¥158.05
items.summary: The dollar index was at 102.26 early on Thursday in Asia; the euro was down 0.15% at $1.1134 and the dollar up 0.14% at ¥158.045. The dollar slipped after Warsh's press conference, and the 2-year Treasury yield was about 4.71%. The ECB and Bank of Japan are both expected to hold rates (Free Malaysia Today, 29 Oct).

items.title: Gold slips about 1% to near $4,038; silver near $53.15
items.summary: Spot gold fell nearly 1% to about $4,044 an ounce early on Thursday and was below $4,038 by 05:14 SAST; silver fell as much as 1.5% to about $53.15 (GoodReturns, 29 Oct). Traders are waiting for today's US PCE inflation data.

items.title: Asia: KOSPI down 2.6%; Samsung falls over 4% despite record profit
items.summary: MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan fell 0.7%, the KOSPI 2.6% after a nearly 7% jump on Wednesday and China's blue chips 0.9%, while the Nikkei rose 0.3% and the Hang Seng 0.2%. Samsung Electronics fell more than 4% even though third-quarter operating profit rose nearly ninefold to a record; SK Hynix rose 1.3% (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct).

items.title: CART and DASH: $65 deal price is above Instacart's scanner target
items.summary: Instacart (Maplebear) closed at $58.42 on 28 October against a $55.28 LRC Stock Scanner target; the $65 offer is about 11% above that close (DoorDash, 29 Oct). DoorDash closed at $169.50 against a $141.80 target (LRC Stock Scanner, 28 Oct). Both are HOLDs on the LRC Stock Scanner; ratings unchanged.

items.title: NOW: premarket drop of about 19% would take ServiceNow below its trigger level
items.summary: ServiceNow earned $0.27 a share against $0.35 expected on revenue of $4.1 billion, and was quoted at $122.00 before the open, down 18.6% from its $150.13 close (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct). That is below the $149.40 trigger level on the LRC Stock Scanner but above the $99.11 target. NOW is a HOLD; rating unchanged.

items.title: LLY: beat lifts shares further above the scanner target
items.summary: Lilly closed at $1,288.30 on 28 October and was quoted at $1,350.00 before the open, up 4.7% (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct), well above the $1,065 LRC Stock Scanner target. LLY is a HOLD; rating unchanged.

items.title: GOOGL: about 10% after-hours fall would take Alphabet below its scanner target
items.summary: Alphabet closed at $323.10 on 28 October (LRC Stock Scanner) before falling about 10% after hours on its profit miss and negative free cash flow (Reuters via Investing.com, 28 Oct); a 10% fall would put it near $291, below the scanner's $314.70 target. GOOGL is a HOLD on the LRC Stock Scanner; rating unchanged.

items.title: MSFT: up about 3% after hours; capex below plan
items.summary: Microsoft rose 2.7% after hours (Investing.com, 28 Oct), smaller than the roughly 5% first reported, as capex of $45.2 billion came in below expectations (Stocktwits, 28 Oct). It closed at $527.90 (LRC Stock Scanner, 28 Oct); a 3% rise would leave it below the $561.20 scanner target. MSFT is a HOLD; rating unchanged.

items.title: AMZN and INTC report today
items.summary: Amazon reports its September-quarter results on Thursday (Investing.com, 28 Oct). Amazon closed at $252.60, just above its $249.80 scanner target and $247.10 trigger level, and Intel at $93.88 against an $86.22 target (LRC Stock Scanner, 28 Oct). Both are HOLDs; ratings unchanged. Microsoft's and Alphabet's capex shortfalls put cloud spending at the centre of Amazon's report.
